title: Valid Parenthesis String
description:
# Valid Parenthesis String

You are given a string `s` containing only `'('`, `')'`, and `'*'`.

Return `true` if there is at least one way to replace every `'*'` so that the final string is a valid parenthesis string. Each `'*'` may become `'('`, become `')'`, or become an empty string.

A valid parenthesis string must satisfy all of these rules:

*   every `'('` has a matching `')'` after it;
*   every `')'` has a matching `'('` before it;
*   matched parentheses are properly nested.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "()"
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The string is already balanced.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "(*)"
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The `'*'` can be empty.

## Example 3:

**Input:** s = "(*))"
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The `'*'` can become `'('`, producing `(())`.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 100`
*   `s[i]` is `'('`, `')'`, or `'*'`.

solutions.name: Greedy Possible Balance Range
solutions.description:
## Approach
Maintain a range `[low, high]` of possible unmatched opening-parenthesis counts after each prefix. A real `'('` raises both bounds, a real `')'` lowers both bounds, and `'*'` lowers `low` but raises `high` because it can act as `')'`, empty, or `'('`. Clamp `low` to zero and fail if `high` becomes negative.

## Key Insight
The exact set of possible balances is always a continuous range. `high < 0` means even treating all flexible characters as openings cannot save the prefix. At the end, `low == 0` means zero unmatched openings is one of the reachable balances.

## Complexity Analysis
The algorithm scans the string once, so the time complexity is O(n). It stores only two counters, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Two Stack Index Matching
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store indices of real `'('` characters in one stack and indices of `'*'` characters in another stack. A `')'` first matches a real opening if possible, otherwise a previous star can act as `'('`. After the scan, every remaining real opening must be matched by a later star acting as `')'`.

## Key Insight
A star can replace a missing parenthesis only if its index is on the correct side of the pair it is forming. The second phase is necessary because an earlier star cannot close a later opening parenthesis.

## Complexity Analysis
The string is scanned once and each index is pushed and popped at most once, so the time complexity is O(n). The stacks may hold O(n) indices.

solutions.name: Top-Down Balance Memoization
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use DFS over `(index, balance)`, where `balance` is the number of unmatched opening parentheses. A star branches into three choices. Memoization prevents repeated exploration of the same suffix state, and impossible negative or too-large balances are pruned immediately.

## Key Insight
This method models the definition directly: choose one meaning for every star and track whether the final balance can be zero without any prefix going negative. It is slower than greedy, but it exposes the state space that the greedy range compresses.

## Complexity Analysis
There are O(n^2) reachable `(index, balance)` states and each state does constant branching work after memoization. The memo table also uses O(n^2) space.

solutions.name: Bottom-Up Reachable Balance DP
solutions.description:
## Approach
Iteratively maintain a boolean array of reachable balances after each processed prefix. For `'('`, shift balances up; for `')'`, shift balances down when possible; for `'*'`, keep the same balance and also try both shifts. The string is valid if balance zero is reachable after the final character.

## Key Insight
This is the iterative version of the memoized search. It makes every reachable balance explicit, which is useful for teaching before showing how the greedy method compresses the reachable set into one interval.

## Complexity Analysis
There are at most n + 1 balances for each of n characters, so the time complexity is O(n^2). Only the current and next balance arrays are stored, so the space complexity is O(n).

solutions.name: Two-Pass Directional Greedy
solutions.description:
## Approach
Run one pass from left to right, treating every `'*'` as a potential `'('`; this verifies no prefix has too many closing parentheses. Then run one pass from right to left, treating every `'*'` as a potential `')'`; this verifies no suffix has too many opening parentheses.

## Key Insight
A valid assignment must satisfy both directional prefix conditions. The first pass proves every `')'` can be matched by something before it, and the second pass proves every `'('` can be matched by something after it.

## Complexity Analysis
The algorithm scans the string twice, so the time complexity is O(n). It stores only one counter in each pass, so the space complexity is O(1).
